statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of seven paths; source code was not available, so findings are based on rendered/runtime/network evidence.

page.framework: server-rendered multi-page site with client-side enhancement
page.notes: Public French TV guide and entertainment editorial site. Audited homepage, listing, article, programme detail, search entry/results, and 404. Excluded account login, paid subscription checkout after the consent offer, games, podcasts, external streaming providers, and exhaustive channel/date permutations because they are separate domains or repeat covered templates.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot or computed background under an emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark condition will reveal whether surfaces re-tint; the page CSS / a color-scheme declaration is corroborating evidence. The model chooses the method.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is byte-identical to the normal capture and the CSS probe found no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() rules.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video, or an in-page probe of getAnimations()/computed animation under an emulated prefers-reduced-motion: reduce condition, can show whether motion stops. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: On the article, the reduced-motion probe still found three running 1,500 ms shimmer animations and no prefers-reduced-motion rule.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot under emulated prefers-contrast: more / forced-colors, or an axe/contrast probe, can show whether controls and text survive. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: High-contrast emulation remained legible and CSS contains a contrast/forced-colors adaptation signal.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video of a route/state change shows whether it animates; the page source / ::view-transition usage corroborates. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS inspection across the representative templates found no view-transition declarations despite a navigation-heavy MPA.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and representative-path feature/applicability inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked reveal interaction was present on the representative templates, so there is no scroll-linked motion implementation to assess.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, or scroll-linked reveal interaction was present on the representative templates, so there is no scroll-linked motion implementation to assess.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for scroll-snap / overscroll-behavior / physics-based easing vs custom pointermove listeners. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS inspection found native scroll-snap use and no evidence that the programme browsing surface depends on custom pointermove gesture handling.

checkOutcomes.method: a transition video of scrolling, or CSS inspection for scroll-state container queries. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The CSS probe found no scroll-state() rules or scroll progress treatment on the long homepage/article templates.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for anchor-name / position-anchor / position-try on overlays; a screenshot of an open overlay near a viewport edge can show drift. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Five role=dialog overlays are present on the homepage, but CSS inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try rules.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for ::highlight / scroll-marker; a transition video can show whether attention is cued after navigation. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative pages expose breadcrumbs/current hierarchy, descriptive links, sequential headings, and a visible skip-link focus cue.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot on load, or a DOM probe for full-viewport overlays present before interaction. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show the consent notice covering the viewport before the TV guide can be used; the mobile panel occupies almost the entire 360×800 viewport.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM/source inspection for popover / <dialog> / <details> vs custom overlay divs with manual dismiss handling. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The DOM probe found five role=dialog containers, zero dialog elements, and zero popover elements.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot plus layout metrics can show the proportion of the viewport given to chrome vs content. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The first-view screenshots contain policy prose and choice chrome while the actual programme grid is fully hidden or dimmed.

checkOutcomes.method: layout metrics (scrollWidth vs innerWidth) and a screenshot at an emulated narrow mobile viewport reveal overflow. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: At 360×800 the layout primitive measured scrollWidth=clientWidth=360 with zero horizontal overflow and a valid viewport meta.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection for @container / container-type; a computed-style probe of the same component in a wide vs narrow container shows whether it adapts. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS inspection found container-query rules across all representative templates, providing component-level adaptation beyond viewport media queries.

checkOutcomes.method: a focus probe (focus an element, read the computed outline) or an axe target-size check; a screenshot of a focused control corroborates. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The homepage probe found programme/channel links only 12–19 px high, and article breadcrumb/author links 15–21 px high.

checkOutcomes.method: screenshot the first viewport and key scrolled states; inspect heading structure, nav labels, button text, and visual hierarchy; a task walkthrough can show whether the next action is obvious. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: On both desktop and mobile, the first viewport contains only the blocking consent decision; “Programme TV” and its date/channel controls are not available.

checkOutcomes.method: run the flow manually with screenshots/DOM snapshots at each step; compare expected vs actual path length; inspect form requirements, navigation continuity, and blockers. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The notice says users must accept data processing to browse free, while the only refusal path is “Refuser et s’abonner (1,99€)”; the guide behind it cannot be operated.

checkOutcomes.method: exercise network delay/failure, invalid input, empty data and success states; screenshot the state messaging and recovery controls; inspect whether browser history and focus remain sensible. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A real 404 returns HTTP 404, explains the lost signal, and provides a direct “Retourner à la page d’accueil” recovery link; populated search exposes categorized result counts.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse reports LCP/CLS/TBT directly and the model may run it; layout metrics + a layout-shift observer + a long-task observer (the evidence primitives) give the same signal first-party. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 2.7 s (performance 0.93), while the separate trace measured 1.88 s; the variance places the page near rather than consistently inside the ≤2.5 s good range.

checkOutcomes.method: the layout primitive's CLS observer captures shifts; a transition video of the first seconds shows content jumping. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Layout observation and Lighthouse both measured CLS 0 during the tested load.

checkOutcomes.method: the layout primitive records long tasks; a heap summary shows the object population; Lighthouse reports TBT. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The trace recorded zero long tasks and 0 ms TBT; Lighthouse corroborated only 20 ms TBT.

checkOutcomes.method: a HAR summary can reveal cache headers, redirects, render-blocking candidates, weight offenders and dependency shape; a trace/Lighthouse insight report can corroborate LCP discovery, render-blocking, font-display and document latency. The m
checkOutcomes.evidence: The HAR recorded 101 requests; third parties transferred 506,338 bytes, and the summary identified missing cache headers, one uncompressed script, redirects, and parser-inserted consent resources.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse/trace/code-coverage style evidence can flag unused JS/CSS, duplicated JavaScript and legacy code; a HAR summary shows third-party byte cost and request count. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 387 KiB of unused JavaScript, including advertising, Google identity, consent, Datadog RUM, and GraphQL bundles with 53–85% waste.

checkOutcomes.method: axe-core (injectable via the evaluate primitive) or Lighthouse's a11y audits enumerate these; a DOM probe of the accessibility-relevant attributes is a first-party alternative. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The search input has only a placeholder and no label or aria-label; the programme detail probe also found an unnamed watch-action link.

checkOutcomes.method: axe contrast rules, a Lighthouse contrast audit, or an in-page probe computing contrast ratios from computed colours. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found #ff004b/white text at 3.92:1 and grey programme subtitles at 2.95:1, below the 4.5:1 requirement for normal text.

checkOutcomes.method: axe/Lighthouse structural audits; a focus-walk probe (tab through, read activeElement + computed outline) is a first-party alternative. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The templates contain main/nav/header/footer landmarks, sequential headings, a skip link, and a 2 px dashed visible focus outline.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot of body and heading text, plus CSS inspection for text-wrap / text alignment / font fallback handling. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Desktop/mobile screenshots and article heading inspection show readable type, stable hierarchy, and no horizontal text clipping in the measured viewport.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse/axe target-size, meta-viewport and media-caption audits are useful signals; screenshots at narrow and zoomed conditions plus DOM/media inspection can corroborate. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Objective target measurements found many visible links 12–21 px high, despite the page reflowing without horizontal overflow at 360 px.

checkOutcomes.method: capture Runtime/Log CDP events, or a probe that reads collected errors; Lighthouse reports this too. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse captured a Google Identity FedCM NetworkError and “Not signed in with the identity provider” in the console.

checkOutcomes.method: a DOM/source probe for doctype/charset/img dimensions; CSS inspection for repetition; Lighthouse best-practices audits cover the rest. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The images primitive reported width/height attributes missing on all 100 inspected images, increasing maintainability and potential layout-shift risk even though this run’s CLS was zero.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse best-practices audits and DevTools inspector/deprecation signals can surface these; DOM/source probes can verify paste handlers and prompt timing. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found use of the deprecated Shared Storage API in advertising-core/5.215.0/core-ads.js.

checkOutcomes.method: a DOM probe reads <title> and meta[name=description]; Lighthouse SEO audits cover the same ground. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: All six content/search templates inspected expose descriptive titles and meta descriptions; article and programme raw HTML preserve them.

checkOutcomes.method: a DOM probe for anchor hrefs, viewport meta, and robots; Lighthouse SEO audits corroborate. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page has a viewport meta, real href links, permissive robots rules for public content, and 84–100% raw-HTML content coverage.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect response status and headers, <link rel=canonical>, hreflang links, robots meta, robots.txt and sitemap.xml; Lighthouse SEO audits cover several of these. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The invalid route correctly returned HTTP 404 but emitted meta robots “index,follow”; /sitemap.xml returned the full 404 HTML rather than a sitemap.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect JSON-LD/microdata and social preview tags against visible content; Lighthouse has a manual structured-data audit, and ad-hoc probes can parse schema.org blocks. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The Mask Singer page has useful Open Graph tags but no JSON-LD, while the article correctly exposes NewsArticle and BreadcrumbList.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect response headers / page protocol via an evaluate probe or the network layer; Lighthouse best-practices flags HTTPS and CSP issues. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, and nosniff are present, but CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; four cookies were flagged not Secure and/or SameSite=None, including a 395-day analytics cookie.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect network requests and third-party origins; a probe of analytics/beacon calls. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: During the blocked consent state, the page contacted 14 third-party origins; 36 third-party requests transferred 506,338 bytes, including Wysistat, Google identity, Datadog, Facebook, and consent infrastructure.

checkOutcomes.method: a probe for permission requests fired on load; source inspection for passkey / WebAuthn / navigator.credentials usage in auth flows. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No geolocation/notification permission prompt appeared on load across any path; authentication is optional and outside the programme-discovery flow.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect response headers and browser security state; Lighthouse/DevTools security audits can corroborate HSTS, clickjacking, Trusted Types, origin isolation and third-party cookie findings. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Headers inspection found no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; the CSP source lists are broad and allow unsafe execution.

checkOutcomes.method: load with scripting disabled or compare a no-JS fetch of the HTML against the rendered page; check for Baseline-aware fallbacks in source. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw HTML contains 84% of homepage content, 93% of article content, and 100% of programme-detail content; no page is a JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: exercise menus near viewport edges with a screenshot; a probe of async/visibility behaviour. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Menus/overlays rendered within the tested viewport, BFCache passed in Lighthouse, and repeated menu open/close left the DOM node count unchanged.

checkOutcomes.method: a probe for a service worker registration and a web app manifest; test behaviour offline. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page links a standalone web app manifest, but the service-worker probe found zero registrations and no controlling worker.

checkOutcomes.method: simulate failed fetches/offline mode or inspect representative 404/500 routes; screenshots and DOM snapshots of error/loading/empty states show whether recovery is possible. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The tested 404 returns the correct status and a concise recovery action rather than a broken shell or infinite spinner.

checkOutcomes.method: a DOM probe for <html lang>/dir and CSS inspection for logical vs physical properties. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page correctly declares lang=fr, but the stylesheet probe counted 162 physical left/right declarations and only one logical-property use on the homepage.

checkOutcomes.method: source inspection for Intl.* usage vs hand-rolled formatting; a probe of rendered dates/numbers under a different locale. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The document declares French, and programme dates/times and relative day labels are rendered consistently in the French locale across guide and search states.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and representative-path feature/applicability inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited product is a France-only broadcast guide presenting the single local broadcast schedule; no cross-zone event coordination or user-selectable timezone flow was present.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited product is a France-only broadcast guide presenting the single local broadcast schedule; no cross-zone event coordination or user-selectable timezone flow was present.

checkOutcomes.method: a screenshot of consent/upsell/cancel flows; source inspection for declarative button actions vs misleading controls. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The primary button is “Accepter”; the only visible refusal is “Refuser et s’abonner (1,99€)”, and no free reject-all choice is offered alongside acceptance.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and representative-path feature/applicability inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The only authored input in scope is optional search; no required or transactional form submission with validation errors was present.
checkOutcomes.reason: The only authored input in scope is optional search; no required or transactional form submission with validation errors was present.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and representative-path feature/applicability inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No address, payment, sign-in, or sign-up form collecting autofill-eligible personal data was present on the representative paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No address, payment, sign-in, or sign-up form collecting autofill-eligible personal data was present on the representative paths.

checkOutcomes.method: walkthrough checkout/subscription/auth/account flows when present; screenshot pricing, confirmation, cancellation and reauthentication states; inspect passkey/autocomplete support for sign-in and payment. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The first viewport asks for €1.99 to refuse processing while the free path commits the user to extensive personalised advertising purposes.

checkOutcomes.method: inspect transferred image bytes vs displayed size; source inspection for modern formats and resolution handling. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Of 100 images, 78 below-fold images were not lazy-loaded, 23 lacked srcset, eight used legacy formats, and none used AVIF/WebP; all lacked intrinsic dimensions.

checkOutcomes.method: a long-task / network probe for background fetches and processing while idle or backgrounded. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 387 KiB unused JavaScript while the HAR loaded 33 scripts, including ads, identity, monitoring, consent, and duplicate html-load/staging traffic.

checkOutcomes.method: a HAR summary shows third-party bytes, font/media weight and caching; screenshots/video reveal autoplay and decorative media; trace/layout evidence shows whether media/animation keeps work running. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Third parties transferred 506,338 of 1,091,753 bytes (46%) across 36 requests; consent, identity, RUM, and tracking dominate the third-party budget.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and representative-path feature/applicability inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: This public editorial/TV guide exposes crawlable SSR content but no declared agent-facing transactional capability; emerging WebMCP tools are not required for the observed scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: This public editorial/TV guide exposes crawlable SSR content but no declared agent-facing transactional capability; emerging WebMCP tools are not required for the observed scope.

checkOutcomes.method: Recon and representative-path feature/applicability inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation or language-model feature is part of the site’s declared or visible user experience, so an on-device inference implementation is not applicable.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation or language-model feature is part of the site’s declared or visible user experience, so an on-device inference implementation is not applicable.

checkOutcomes.method: compare heap snapshots for retained growth - a baseline, then one taken after repeating the interaction with `--interact` about 10x (the memory-tracer methodology: baseline -> repeat -> post -> compare). Performance.getMetrics (JSHeapUsedSi
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten menu open/close cycles, DOM nodes stayed at 3,095; used heap rose only 447,025 bytes (3.5%), while separate heap snapshots differed by 1.8% self size.

checkOutcomes.method: a single `heap` summary's totals (nodeCount, totalSelfSizeBytes, constructor population) plus Performance.getMetrics (Nodes, JSHeapUsedSize) give the current footprint to judge against the page's purpose. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: The baseline heap summary was 20,974,182 self bytes with 3,095 live DOM elements, proportionate to a dense programme grid and bounded after interaction.

checkOutcomes.method: the `heap` summary by constructor (Detached* nodes) compared across a before/after pair shows a growing detached-DOM population; an `evaluate` probe can sample listener/timer counts (e.g. getEventListeners-style counting, or instrumenting a
checkOutcomes.evidence: Across ten menu cycles, DOM nodes remained 3,095, instrumented listeners had net growth -1, and no intervals were added.

principleOutcomes.reason: The representative public editorial/guide surfaces have no declared agent-facing capability or on-device AI feature; both emerging checks were judged not applicable.

paths.description: Homepage and primary TV-guide grid, representing the core programme-discovery task.
News index, representing editorial listings and pagination.
Current news article, representing long-form editorial detail pages.
Mask Singer programme detail, representing show metadata and watch/discovery actions.
Search entry form, representing the site’s primary query input.
Search for “mask singer”, exercising query submission through a populated results state.
Deliberately invalid route, representing HTTP error messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is byte-identical to the normal capture and the CSS probe found no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens, retaining sufficient contrast in both schemes.

findings.summary: Loading shimmer motion continues under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: On the article, the reduced-motion probe still found three running 1,500 ms shimmer animations and no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove shimmer animation or replace it with a static loading treatment.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use view transitions.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection across the representative templates found no view-transition declarations despite a navigation-heavy MPA.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a progressively enhanced cross-document View Transition for stable page chrome and key shared elements.

findings.summary: Persistent navigation does not expose scroll-state-aware feedback.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no scroll-state() rules or scroll progress treatment on the long homepage/article templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky scroll-state container query or lightweight declarative progress indicator to reduce chrome after scrolling and preserve orientation.

findings.summary: Custom menus and overlays do not use anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: Five role=dialog overlays are present on the homepage, but CSS inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and fallback positions for transient menus near viewport edges.

findings.summary: A full-viewport consent wall obscures the core guide on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show the consent notice covering the viewport before the TV guide can be used; the mobile panel occupies almost the entire 360×800 viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a compact, non-blocking consent choice with an equally prominent free rejection path; defer non-essential tracking until a choice is made.

findings.summary: Overlay UI is built from generic role=dialog containers rather than native overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found five role=dialog containers, zero dialog elements, and zero popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal decisions and popover for transient menus, preserving native focus, top-layer, and dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Consent chrome consumes the entire first viewport instead of prioritising programme content.
findings.evidence: The first-view screenshots contain policy prose and choice chrome while the actual programme grid is fully hidden or dimmed.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the notice to the minimum decision-relevant content and keep the core page visible and usable.

findings.summary: Many primary links have touch targets below recommended dimensions.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found programme/channel links only 12–19 px high, and article breadcrumb/author links 15–21 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary mobile controls, without shrinking visible labels.

findings.summary: The page purpose and primary TV-guide action are hidden on entry.
findings.evidence: On both desktop and mobile, the first viewport contains only the blocking consent decision; “Programme TV” and its date/channel controls are not available.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users see and operate the guide before optional consent, and keep a clearly labelled date/time action visible.

findings.summary: The programme-discovery journey requires accepting tracking or paying before interaction.
findings.evidence: The notice says users must accept data processing to browse free, while the only refusal path is “Refuser et s’abonner (1,99€)”; the guide behind it cannot be operated.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a free reject-non-essential option and allow the core browse/search flow with necessary-only storage.

findings.summary: One Lighthouse run missed the good LCP threshold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 2.7 s (performance 0.93), while the separate trace measured 1.88 s; the variance places the page near rather than consistently inside the ≤2.5 s good range.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource and defer consent, identity, advertising, and monitoring scripts that compete during startup.

findings.summary: Startup delivery includes avoidable third-party chains and weak cache hygiene.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 101 requests; third parties transferred 506,338 bytes, and the summary identified missing cache headers, one uncompressed script, redirects, and parser-inserted consent resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional scripts, remove redirects, compress text, set durable cache headers for versioned assets, and keep critical dependency chains short.

findings.summary: The homepage ships substantial JavaScript unused during the initial task.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 387 KiB of unused JavaScript, including advertising, Google identity, consent, Datadog RUM, and GraphQL bundles with 53–85% waste.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load identity, ads, monitoring, and feature bundles only when the relevant feature or consent state requires them.

findings.summary: Search and programme controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: The search input has only a placeholder and no label or aria-label; the programme detail probe also found an unnamed watch-action link.
findings.suggestedFix: Add persistent labels or aria-labelledby for search and explicit accessible names for icon-only actions.

findings.summary: Several guide labels fail WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found #ff004b/white text at 3.92:1 and grey programme subtitles at 2.95:1, below the 4.5:1 requirement for normal text.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the brand red for small text states and use a darker neutral for secondary programme labels.

findings.summary: Small link hit areas reduce usability under touch and zoom.
findings.evidence: Objective target measurements found many visible links 12–21 px high, despite the page reflowing without horizontal overflow at 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add padding or minimum block-size to links so zoom and touch users retain comfortably sized controls.

findings.summary: The page logs identity errors during a normal unauthenticated load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a Google Identity FedCM NetworkError and “Not signed in with the identity provider” in the console.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat unauthenticated identity state as expected control flow and avoid logging it as an error.

findings.summary: Images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reported width/height attributes missing on all 100 inspected images, increasing maintainability and potential layout-shift risk even though this run’s CLS was zero.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height (or an equivalent reserved aspect ratio) for every content image at render time.

findings.summary: Advertising code uses a deprecated browser API.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found use of the deprecated Shared Storage API in advertising-core/5.215.0/core-ads.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Upgrade or remove the advertising integration before the API is removed, and keep third-party bundles on supported platform APIs.

findings.summary: Indexing signals include an indexable 404 and no sitemap at the conventional location.
findings.evidence: The invalid route correctly returned HTTP 404 but emitted meta robots “index,follow”; /sitemap.xml returned the full 404 HTML rather than a sitemap.
findings.suggestedFix: Set noindex on error pages and publish a sitemap index at /sitemap.xml (or advertise its actual URL in robots.txt).

findings.summary: The programme detail lacks structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The Mask Singer page has useful Open Graph tags but no JSON-LD, while the article correctly exposes NewsArticle and BreadcrumbList.
findings.suggestedFix: Add schema.org TVSeries/CreativeWork and breadcrumb JSON-LD matching the visible programme details and watch availability.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP settings weaken otherwise secure HTTPS transport.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, and nosniff are present, but CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; four cookies were flagged not Secure and/or SameSite=None, including a 395-day analytics cookie.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline with nonces or hashes, and set Secure plus an appropriate Lax/Strict SameSite policy on first-party cookies.

findings.summary: Tracking and identity traffic starts before an affirmative consent choice.
findings.evidence: During the blocked consent state, the page contacted 14 third-party origins; 36 third-party requests transferred 506,338 bytes, including Wysistat, Google identity, Datadog, Facebook, and consent infrastructure.
findings.suggestedFix: Before consent, load only necessary consent assets; defer analytics, identity, social, advertising, and RUM until their purpose is accepted.

findings.summary: Several defensive browser policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; the CSP source lists are broad and allow unsafe execution.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or stricter), a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and tighten CSP origins.

findings.summary: The installable manifest is not backed by an active service worker or offline fallback.
findings.evidence: The page links a standalone web app manifest, but the service-worker probe found zero registrations and no controlling worker.
findings.suggestedFix: If installability is intended, register a small service worker with an offline shell/fallback; otherwise avoid implying a standalone offline-capable app.

findings.summary: Styles are dominated by physical direction properties.
findings.evidence: The page correctly declares lang=fr, but the stylesheet probe counted 162 physical left/right declarations and only one logical-property use on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use margin/padding/inset-inline and inline/block sizing so components can adapt if translated to RTL or alternate writing modes.

findings.summary: The consent choice presents acceptance as free and refusal as paid.
findings.evidence: The primary button is “Accepter”; the only visible refusal is “Refuser et s’abonner (1,99€)”, and no free reject-all choice is offered alongside acceptance.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer accept and reject-non-essential choices with equal prominence, plain language, and no financial penalty for privacy.

findings.summary: The paid-refusal subscription commitment is embedded in the blocking privacy decision.
findings.evidence: The first viewport asks for €1.99 to refuse processing while the free path commits the user to extensive personalised advertising purposes.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate subscription sales from privacy consent and expose price, term, cancellation, and a free necessary-only route without coercion.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses several efficiency basics.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 78 below-fold images were not lazy-loaded, 23 lacked srcset, eight used legacy formats, and none used AVIF/WebP; all lacked intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold images, emit responsive srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions, and negotiate AVIF/WebP while retaining fallbacks.

findings.summary: Optional bundles perform wasteful startup work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 387 KiB unused JavaScript while the HAR loaded 33 scripts, including ads, identity, monitoring, consent, and duplicate html-load/staging traffic.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional work by feature and consent state, remove staging/redirected loaders, and schedule non-critical processing after user-visible work.

findings.summary: Third parties consume nearly half of transferred bytes before the core task starts.
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 506,338 of 1,091,753 bytes (46%) across 36 requests; consent, identity, RUM, and tracking dominate the third-party budget.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and defer or remove integrations that do not directly support programme discovery.

taskList.title: Provide a free, equal-prominence reject option and remove the blocking consent wall
Defer and remove unused third-party JavaScript before the core guide loads
Tighten CSP, cookie flags, and browser defense headers
Fix accessible names, contrast, and touch target sizing
Modernise responsive image delivery and reserve image space
Add preference-driven dark and reduced-motion treatments
Correct indexing metadata for 404s, sitemap, and programme entities
Replace custom overlays with dialog/popover and anchor positioning
